name: Christopher Columbus
summary: First voyage across the Atlantic to the Caribbean, sailing for Castile.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Late 15th century.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: About 90 men spread across three ships.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Born in a maritime republic in what is now Italy.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: The flagship was a carrack called Santa María.

hints.label: Backing
hints.text: Funded by the Catholic Monarchs of Castile and Aragón, aiming for Asia but landing in the Caribbean.

name: Ferdinand Magellan
summary: Led the Spanish expedition that completed the first circumnavigation of the globe, though he died along the way.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Early 16th century.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: About 270 men set out; fewer than 20 sailed home on the one surviving ship.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Portuguese-born, but sailing under another crown.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: A fleet of five ships: Trinidad, San Antonio, Concepción, Victoria and Santiago.

hints.label: Fate
hints.text: He was killed in the Philippines; his deputy Elcano brought the Victoria home.

name: James Cook
summary: First Pacific voyage: observed the transit of Venus at Tahiti, charted New Zealand and the east coast of Australia.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Late 18th century.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: About 94 people aboard, including scientists and artists.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: From the British Isles; a farm labourer's son who rose through the navy.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: A converted coal ship named Endeavour.

hints.label: Mission
hints.text: To observe the transit of Venus from the Pacific, then search for a great southern continent.

name: Vasco da Gama
summary: Opened the sea route from Europe to India around the southern tip of Africa.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Late 15th century.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: Roughly 170 men in four vessels.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Portuguese, sent by his king.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: The flagship was the São Gabriel.

hints.label: Goal
hints.text: Reach the spice markets of India by sea, going around Africa.

name: Roald Amundsen
summary: Led the first expedition to reach the South Pole, beating a British rival by about five weeks.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Early 20th century.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: A small party of just 19 men.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Norwegian.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: The ship Fram, already famous for Arctic drift expeditions.

hints.label: Method
hints.text: He reached the southern geographic pole with sled dogs and skis, ahead of a British team.

name: Ernest Shackleton
summary: The Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition: the ship was crushed by pack ice, yet every man survived.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Early 20th century, during the First World War.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: 28 men, including one stowaway.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Born in Ireland to an Anglo-Irish family, sailing from Britain.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: A wooden ship named Endurance, crushed by ice in the Weddell Sea.

hints.label: Outcome
hints.text: The planned continental crossing never began, but a small lifeboat voyage to South Georgia saved everyone.

name: Zheng He
summary: Admiral of the Ming dynasty's treasure fleets, which sailed across the Indian Ocean to Arabia and East Africa.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Early 15th century.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: Fleets of tens of thousands of men; the first voyage carried roughly 27,000.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Chinese, serving the Ming court.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: Giant 'treasure ships' leading fleets of more than 60 vessels.

hints.label: Background
hints.text: A court admiral of Muslim Yunnanese origin whose voyages reached the coast of East Africa.

name: Leif Erikson
summary: Norse voyage from Greenland to a land the sagas call Vinland, probably the northern tip of Newfoundland.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Around the year 1000.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: A crew of roughly 35 men.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Norse, born in Iceland and based in Greenland.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: A Norse seagoing cargo ship (a knarr).

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: He reached North America about 500 years before the better-known Atlantic crossing, and called the new land Vinland.

name: Marco Polo
summary: A 24-year, 15,000-mile journey along the Silk Road to China, where he served in the court of Kublai Khan before returning to Venice and chronicling his adventures in The Travels of Marco Polo.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Late 13th century

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: Core group of 3 people, mostly family

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Venetian merchant, explorer, and writer

hints.label: Sightings
hints.text: He described seeing unicorns, which modern historians know were actually Asian rhinoceroses

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: While imprisoned, the explorer dictated his lifetime of travel memories to a fellow inmate, who compiled them into a famous manuscript

name: Ibn Battuta
summary: Ibn Battuta's voyage across north Africa to Cairo

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Early 14th century

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: Traveled alone starting from Tangier, eventually joiingin a large travel caravan.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Muslim traveller, explorer, and scholar from Tangier, Morocco.

hints.label: Sightings
hints.text: He met around 60 heads of state, serving as a legal judge in Delhi, India, and an envoy to China.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: Over 29 years (beginning in 1325), he journeyed roughly 75,000 miles, spanning across more than 40 modern countries.

name: Hanno
summary: Hanno's naval exploration of the western coast of Africa

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Around 5th century BC

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: 30,000 people

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: Carthage, or modern day Tunisia

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: 60 ships

hints.label: Sightings
hints.text: This explorer thought Gorillas were a race of humans and tried to capture some.

name: Thor Heyerdahl
summary: A 1947 journey by raft across the Pacific Ocean from South America to the Polynesian islands, led by Norwegian explorer and ethnographer Thor Heyerdahl.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Mid 20th century

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: Six-man crew, five of whom were Norwegian

hints.label: Funding
hints.text: The trip was funded by private loans, along with donations of equipment from the United States Army.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: Traveled by raft amde out of balsa logs, which was named after the Inca god Viracocha.

hints.label: Background
hints.text: The purpose of the expedition was to show that indigenous South Americans could have reached Polynesia during pre-Columbian times by drifting with the wind directions and only by using the materials available to those people in their time.

name: William of Rubruck
summary: A Franciscan friar's journey from the eastern Mediterranean to the Mongol court at Karakorum.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Mid-13th century.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: A Flemish Franciscan friar who traveled as a missionary.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: He crossed the Black Sea steppes and Central Asia to reach the Mongol capital.

hints.label: Destination
hints.text: Karakorum, the Mongol Empire's capital.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: His account became one of the most detailed European descriptions of the Mongol world.

name: David Livingstone
summary: Livingstone's trans-African expedition from the upper Zambezi to the Atlantic coast and back to the Indian Ocean.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Mid-19th century.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: A Scottish missionary, physician, and explorer.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: He crossed southern-central Africa from the Zambezi basin to the Atlantic.

hints.label: Landmark
hints.text: He publicized the great waterfall he named Victoria Falls.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: His journeys helped make the interior of southern Africa better known to Europeans.

name: Nain Singh Rawat
summary: A pioneering survey journey across Tibet from Ladakh to Lhasa, made while disguised as a Tibetan pilgrim.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: 19th century.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: An Indian surveyor from Kumaon in the Himalayas.

hints.label: Disguise
hints.text: He traveled as a Buddhist lama and used prayer beads to count his paces.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: His surveys crossed the high plateau between Ladakh and Lhasa.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: His measurements greatly improved maps of Tibet and Central Asia.

name: Pytheas
summary: A Greek voyage from Massalia into the Atlantic, describing Britain and the far-northern land he called Thule.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: 4th century BC.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: A Greek geographer and explorer from Massalia, now Marseille.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: He sailed beyond the Strait of Gibraltar into the Atlantic and north toward Britain.

hints.label: Destination
hints.text: He described a distant northern place called Thule, whose location remains debated.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: His lost account recorded observations of tides, daylight, and northern peoples.

name: Lewis and Clark
summary: The Corps of Discovery traveled from the Mississippi River across the continent to the Pacific Northwest and back.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Early 19th century.

hints.label: Purpose
hints.text: The journey sought a practical water route across the continent to the Pacific.

hints.label: Crew
hints.text: The expedition included soldiers, boatmen, and Shoshone guide Sacagawea.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: They followed the Missouri River, crossed the Rocky Mountains, and descended the Columbia River.

hints.label: Destination
hints.text: They reached the Pacific coast near the mouth of the Columbia River.

name: Jacques Cartier
summary: Cartier's second voyage explored the St. Lawrence River as far inland as the settlements of Stadacona and Hochelaga.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: 16th century.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: A French navigator from Saint-Malo.

hints.label: Vessel
hints.text: He sailed with three ships on his second voyage.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: He entered the Gulf of St. Lawrence and sailed upriver toward present-day Montreal.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: His voyages helped establish France's claims in what became Canada.

name: Alexander the Great
summary: Alexander's campaigns carried his army from Macedonia through Egypt and Persia to the Indus Valley.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: 4th century BC.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: King of Macedon and commander of a large Greek-led army.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: His campaign crossed Asia Minor, the Levant, Egypt, Mesopotamia, and Persia.

hints.label: Landmark
hints.text: He founded Alexandria in Egypt, which became a major center of the ancient world.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: His conquests spread Greek language and culture across a vast region.

name: Sir Edmund Hillary
summary: New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay made the first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: 20th century.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: A New Zealand beekeeper and mountaineer.

hints.label: Team
hints.text: He reached the summit with Sherpa climber Tenzing Norgay.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: The expedition approached Everest from Nepal and established a high camp on the South Col.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: After the ascent, he supported education and health projects in Nepal through the Himalayan Trust.

name: Samuel de Champlain
summary: French explorer Champlain traveled the St. Lawrence and founded Quebec City, later exploring the lake that bears his name.

hints.label: Era
hints.text: Early 17th century.

hints.label: Origin
hints.text: A French navigator, cartographer, and colonist.

hints.label: Route
hints.text: He explored the St. Lawrence River and traveled inland to a lake later named in his honor.

hints.label: Settlement
hints.text: He founded Quebec City in 1608.

hints.label: Legacy
hints.text: He became a central figure in the early French settlement of Canada.
